description: How dwarf people talk to the captain at a station.

dw-back: Pull up a stool. It's in better shape than the last.
Good. I was beginning to wonder.
I'll not charge you to sit.
rumour: Between us and the walls, nobody can name the metal in the gates. A people ought to know where its metal came from.
dw-heard: The word in the shafts is that
A hauler told me, and he was sober, that
I read it in a manifest, so it's probably true:
dw-coda: Worth a note in your ledger.
Prices will follow, you mark me.
I'd not stake a contract on it.
no-rumour: Quiet shift. I'd not pad it.
If I knew, I'd sell it. I don't.
No news. Doesn't mean there's none.
dw-lead: Right. Here's the shape of it:
dw-workcoda: Read the terms before you sign.
no-work: Not a thing. Try the board.
No contracts that I'd put my name to.
dw-life: I've been paid fair and paid late, and the second is more common.
{system} is solid rock, which suits me.
Twenty years under {faction}, and no complaints in writing.
I mind my work and my invoices.
My hold would have me home, but pay is pay.
dw-thanks: Aye, thanks. I'll mark it a favour.
Good ale's not cheap, so thanks.
dw-toast: To fair weight and honest measure.
To {system}, and the cheap rock under it.
drink-again: I'll not, thanks. I've a clear head to keep.
No more. I'm on the clock, in a manner of speaking.
Put it on the ledger for another day.
pestered: That's a lot of questions for one cup.
I'm not paid by the question.
Mm. Don't you have your own business?
cold: I don't do business with you.
farewell: See you on the next contract.
haggle-no: No. But it was well tried.
The rate stands. I enjoyed that, though.
Not a credit more. Try again next job.
No. It's fair, and you know it.
haggle-offended: There's a line, and you've stood on it. Done.
Now you're not bargaining, you're begging. Finished.
No. I'll find someone with manners.
